overview.description: Kansas City Lowball (also known as Deuce-to-Seven Lowball) is a prestigious poker variant where the *worst* traditional poker hand wins. It uses 'Deuce-to-Seven' ranking: Aces are high and undesirable, and straights and flushes are counted against the player. The goal is to make the lowest possible five-card hand that is not a straight or flush. It is renowned for being the 'purist's lowball' and is a staple of the World Series of Poker.

history.origins: Developed in the mid-20th century in the poker rooms of Kansas City and later Las Vegas. It was designed to provide a more difficult strategic challenge than 'California Lowball' (Ace-to-Five).
timeline: 1950s: Emerges as a high-stakes professional game.
1970s: Included in the World Series of Poker (WSOP) as a $10,000 championship event.
1990s: Popularity spikes among high-stakes 'Mixed Game' players.
Present: Remains the standard for high-stakes lowball poker worldwide.
history.evolution: The transition from 'Single Draw' (one chance to exchange) to 'Triple Draw' (three chances) in modern years has added layers of betting and complexity.
history.cultural: Often called 'The Great Game' by professionals due to the intense psychological pressure and the high value of 'snowshoeing' (bluffing with a bad hand).

setup.players: Up to 7 players. Played with Blinds (Small and Big).
setup.equipment: Standard cards, poker chips, dealer button.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards face down. In Single Draw, there is one exchange phase; in Triple Draw, there are three.

rules.objective: Have the 'lowest' hand at the showdown, where straights and flushes are considered high (bad).
rules.gameplay: 1. Players receive 5 cards. 2. First betting round. 3. Draw phase: Players discard any number of cards and receive replacements. 4. Second betting round (Check/Bet/Raise/Fold). 5. (In Triple Draw, repeat steps 3-4 twice more). 6. **Showdown**: Lowest hand wins the pot.
keyRules: Hand rankings are inverted: worst poker hand wins
Aces are always HIGH (above King) - very bad for low
Straights and flushes count as high hands - avoid them
Best possible hand: 7-5-4-3-2 (unsuited) - 'The Wheel' or 'Number One'
Pairs, trips, quads are very bad hands
Blinds: Small Blind and Big Blind start the action
No qualifier needed - any five cards can win

strategy.basic: Do not draw to a straight or flush. If you have 3-4-5-6, drawing a 2 or 7 will GIVE you a straight, which is essentially a losing hand. Aim for 'disconnected' low cards like 2-3-5-7.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Smooth' hand: A 9-7-6-4-2 is 'smooth' because it is much lower than a 9-8-7-6-2. 'Smoothness' refers to how low your second and third cards are.
strategy.advanced: Snowing: A powerful bluff where you stand pat (don't draw any cards) despite having a pair or a high card. If you act confident, players with legitimate 9s or 10s may fold, thinking you have a 7 or 8.
tips: In Single Draw, don't enter the pot unless you can draw just 1 or 2 cards to a 9-low or better.
The Deuce (2) is the most important card in your hand. Without it, your hand is significantly more vulnerable to being out-lowed.

difficulty.easy: Draws to straights/flushes by mistake; fails to bluff; poor starting hand selection.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable 'Smoothness' evaluation; basic drawing strategy for Triple Draw.
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'Snowing' and detecting bluffs; perfectly calculates the range of opponent hands based on their discard count (e.g., 'Drawing 1' vs 'Drawing 3').

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.

synthesis.shortDescription: A prestigious poker variant where the worst traditional hand wins. Deuce-to-Seven ranking with straights and flushes counting against you. A staple of high-stakes poker.

prompts.human: Welcome to Kansas City Lowball! In this game, the WORST hand wins. Aces are high (bad!), and you want to avoid straights and flushes. The best hand is 7-5-4-3-2. Can you build the 'worst' hand and outplay your opponents?
prompts.ai: Game: Kansas City Lowball (Deuce-to-Seven). Type: Poker Lowball. Hand: 5 cards. Objective: Lowest hand wins. Rules: Aces high (bad), straights/flushes count against. Best hand: 7-5-4-3-2 unsuited. One or three draw rounds. Standard poker betting.

scoring.description: Standard poker pot betting. Winner takes all.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest hand at showdown wins the pot. Hand evaluated by Deuce-to-Seven ranking.
scoring.splitRules: If two players have identical low hands, they split the pot equally.
